headline: The dollar came off, vol deflated and oil cracked — the first honest release of last week's funding squeeze, but a 2.63% real yield, an inverted VIX curve and a 153 SKEW say this is relief, not repair.
summary: Three things moved in the right direction at once today, and they are all the same trade. DXY -0.4% to 101.86 after Friday's 102.28, with USDKRW -0.7%, USDINR -0.6%, USDMXN -0.6% and USDCNY -0.4% — the funding squeeze that defined last week is finally paying out instead of compounding. VIX -9.4% to 23.23, VIX3M -3.7%, MOVE -5.3% to 92.77. Europe and Asia took the hint: Euro Stoxx +1.5%, DAX +1.2% (89th percentile of its year), CAC +1.0%, Nikkei +2.3%, TAIEX +4.9%. Risk regime improves to -15 from -23, and credit & vol, still the worst composite, improves to -63 from -66. The difference versus Friday matters: Friday's bounce was funded by liquidating defensives; today's is funded by the dollar.

The second big move is oil breaking. Brent -4.2% to 94.18 and now -10.1% on the month; WTI -3.9% to 87.26; RBOB gasoline -18.0% on the month at z=-1.69 and 11.4% below its 200-day. Oil/gold -5.2% in a day. That is a straight transfer to the consumer and it keeps the inflation side quiet — 5y breakevens 2.29 (23rd percentile), 10y 2.23 (16th percentile), both rolling over. It is also a bill coming due for the only sector that has actually worked: XLE is still +40.6% YTD and only -2.7% on the month, with XOP -14.7% and OIH -13.5% in a week. Energy equities have not marked to a $94 Brent. USDCAD +0.6% on a down-dollar day is the corroborating tell.

Nothing structural has been fixed. As of Friday's close the 2y is 4.51 (+5bp), the 10y 4.86, the 30y 5.26 and the 10y real yield 2.63 — 74th percentile, +70bp YTD. 2s10s is 35bp at the 28th percentile and rolling over, 3m10y -39bp on the month, the 30y mortgage 7.18% at the 85th percentile. Duration still isn't hedging equity. The option surface agrees: VIX/VIX3M at 1.0423 is still inverted in the 82nd percentile, and SKEW rose to 153.55, +8.3% on the month — someone is buying tails into falling spot vol. Credit refuses to confirm: HYG/IEF -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, HYG at the 41st percentile and flat on the month. And the factor damage is historic, not a dip: MTUM -20.9% 1m at z=-3.79, high-beta/low-vol -23.5% at z=-3.64, growth/value -15.5% at z=-3.62, SOXX -29.7% at z=-3.2, MU -36.6%, AVGO at the 1st percentile of its 52-week range, CAT -31.2% at z=-3.52 and the 3rd percentile.

The money is in the dispersion, and it widened again. India keeps compounding — Sensex +11.9% on the month at z=2.86 with acceleration 2.66, INDA +10.4%, financed by USDINR -3.0% at z=-2.91. Mexico's IPC sits at the 98th percentile, +10.4% on the month. Against that, Brazil is the one asset still accelerating the wrong way on a down-dollar day: USDBRL 5.5169, +9.9% on the month at z=2.87, trend turning up, acceleration 2.2, with EWZ -24.5% and Bovespa acceleration z=-4.07. Korea is the other wreck — KOSPI -14.3% on the week and -24.3% on the month at z=-3.25, 23.7% below its 200-day — though EWY +4.1% and TAIEX +4.9% show the squeeze reaching even there. Domestically the defensive/value engine is still intact but stretched: RSP/SPY +8.4% on the month at an absurd z=4.16, XLP +10.3%, XLV +9.5%, XLF +6.3%, HD +20.2%, MCD +19.8% at z=3.84. Own the spread, not the index.

good.text: Dollar finally relents: DXY -0.4% to 101.86 with USDKRW -0.7%, USDINR -0.6% (1m z=-2.91), USDMXN -0.6%, USDCNY -0.4%. EM funding pressure is draining, not building.
Vol complex deflating across the board: VIX -9.4% to 23.23, VIX3M -3.7%, term structure -5.5%, MOVE -5.3% to 92.77. Bond vol leading equity vol lower is the right sequence.
Oil breaking is disinflation: Brent -4.2% to 94.18 (-10.1% 1m), WTI -3.9%, gasoline -18.0% on the month. Breakevens sit at 2.29 and 2.23, near 52-week lows.
Breadth and the value/defensive engine still working: RSP/SPY +8.4% 1m at z=4.16, equal-weight +2.6%, XLF +6.3%, XLV +9.5%, IWD +2.7% at the 89th percentile.
Non-US leadership broadening on the weaker dollar: Euro Stoxx +1.5%, DAX +1.2% at the 89th percentile, Sensex +11.9% 1m at z=2.86, Mexico IPC at the 98th percentile.
Metals bid back: copper +1.7%, gold +1.3% to 4127.9, silver +1.6%, platinum +1.3%, with GDX/gold at the 78th percentile and turning up, NEM +13.4% on the week.

bad.text: The vol curve is still inverted while spot falls — VIX/VIX3M 1.0423 at the 82nd percentile and SKEW 153.55, +8.3% on the month. Tail demand is rising into a calmer tape.
Credit won't confirm: HYG/IEF -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, HYG flat on the month at the 41st percentile. Credit & vol is still the worst composite at -63.
The discount rate is still hostile: 10y real yield 2.63 (+70bp YTD, 74th percentile), 30y 5.26, 2s10s 35bp at the 28th percentile and rolling over, 30y mortgage 7.18%.
Momentum and high-beta are in a 3-sigma liquidation, not a pullback: MTUM z=-3.79, high-beta/low-vol z=-3.64, growth/value z=-3.62, SMH/SPY z=-3.48, SOXX -29.7% 1m.
Brazil is the one thing accelerating the wrong way on a down-dollar day: USDBRL 5.5169, +9.9% 1m at z=2.87 with acceleration 2.2, EWZ -24.5% 1m, Bovespa acceleration z=-4.07.
The AI-capex and power chain keeps bleeding under the squeeze: CAT -31.2% 1m at the 3rd percentile, ETN -20.8% (z=-2.92), GEV -22.3%, GRID -14.2%, NLR -16.0% at the 5th percentile, VST -25.1%.

trades.name: Long India vs short broad EM
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: the only EM with a tailwind FX
trades.expr: Long INDA, short an equal dollar amount of EEM. Size 1:1; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: EEM/SPY at z=-1.64 is a blended average hiding a 35-point internal gap. India has a falling USD/INR, accelerating local equities and no semiconductor concentration; EEM is one-third Korea/Taiwan semis plus a Brazil accident.
trades.trigger: INDA +10.4% 1m at z=2.35 with acceleration 2.91 and Sensex +11.9% 1m at z=2.86, while EEM is -11.9% 1m at z=-2.49 and USDBRL is still accelerating at z=2.87.
trades.stop: A sustained semis squeeze that drags SMH/SPY back above -10% on the month, or USDINR turning back up through 95.5.
trades.target: 800bp of spread over the next quarter; INDA relative strength vs S&P from +16.7% toward +25%.

trades.name: Short E&P into the oil break
trades.line: Short XOP: Brent -10.1% 1m, energy equities haven't marked
trades.expr: Short XOP outright, or buy XLE Jan puts ~5% OTM. Hedge beta with a small SPY long if you want pure crude exposure.
trades.thesis: Equity has lagged the crude move badly. XLE is still +40.6% YTD and only -2.7% on the month while Brent is -10.1% and gasoline -18.0%. Cash flow guidance resets lower at $94 Brent and $87 WTI; the 3m relative strength of +13.1% is the cushion that gets taken out first.
trades.trigger: Today's -4.2% in Brent to 94.18 and -3.9% in WTI to 87.26, after XOP -14.7% and OIH -13.5% in a week, with RBOB at z=-1.69 and 11.4% below its 200-day. USDCAD +0.6% on a down-dollar day confirms the oil channel.
trades.stop: Brent reclaiming 100 or XOP closing back above its 200-day (currently ~1.9% below spot) for two sessions.
trades.target: XOP down 12-15% to the low 150s; XLE relative strength vs S&P back to flat on 3 months.

trades.name: Fade the inverted VIX curve
trades.line: Short Dec VIX future vs long Feb: monetize the 1.04 inversion
trades.expr: Short front-month VIX future, long the Feb contract, roughly vega-matched; or sell a VIX Dec 25 call and buy a Feb 25 call.
trades.thesis: Spot vol is deflating (VIX 23.23, -9.4%) while VIX/VIX3M is still 1.0423, the 82nd percentile. Historically that inversion resolves by the front collapsing, not the back rising. The structure pays if the squeeze keeps unwinding and loses only slowly if it doesn't.
trades.trigger: VIX -9.4%, VIX3M -3.7%, MOVE -5.3% to 92.77, and DXY -0.4% — the funding driver of the vol bid is reversing while term structure has not yet renormalized.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M pushing above 1.10 or VIX closing back above 30; SKEW above 160 with HYG making new lows.
trades.target: Term structure back to 0.95 contango, VIX into the 17-18 area.

trades.name: Long USD/BRL
trades.line: Long USDBRL: only EM FX still accelerating as DXY falls
trades.expr: Long USD/BRL spot or 3m forward; alternatively short EWZ against a long EEM leg if you need equity expression.
trades.thesis: Relative weakness on a strong day is the cleanest signal on the board. Every other EM currency rallied against a falling dollar today; the real did not. That is idiosyncratic, and the equity market agrees with EWZ -24.5% on the month.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +0.2% to 5.5169 with DXY -0.4%; 1m move z=2.87, acceleration 2.2, trend turning up, 89th percentile of the year. Bovespa acceleration z=-4.07 and EWZ z=-3.25.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.40, or EWZ reclaiming its 200-day (13.5% above spot is far, so use the FX level).
trades.target: 5.85 on the cross; another 10-12% of EWZ underperformance vs EEM.

trades.name: Gold miners over bullion
trades.line: Long GDX vs short GLD: miners leading metal, margins widening
trades.expr: Long GDX (or GDXJ for more beta), short a dollar-equal GLD. Add NEM as the single-name kicker.
trades.thesis: Miners are outperforming the metal through a gold correction — the classic signature of margin expansion as energy costs collapse. Brent -10.1% on the month is a direct input cost cut for the entire complex.
trades.trigger: GDX/gold +3.4% on the month at the 78th percentile, turning up with acceleration 1.11; GDX +13.6% and GDXJ +13.4% on the week while gold is -2.1% on the month; NEM +13.4% weekly. Gold +1.3% today to 4127.9 on the softer dollar.
trades.stop: GDX/gold back below the 60th percentile, or gold breaking under 3,900 with miners failing to hold.
trades.target: Another 8-10% of relative gain; GDX back above its 200-day (2.99% above spot).

trades.name: Short HY credit vs loans
trades.line: Short HYG vs long BKLN: spread risk without the duration bet
trades.expr: Short HYG, long BKLN roughly dollar-neutral. Pure credit-quality and duration expression, no rates view.
trades.thesis: HY is the asset that never participated in two separate equity bounces. HYG/IEF is -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, while loans sit at the 92nd percentile with a floating coupon. If the vol regime re-tightens, HY gaps and loans don't; if it calms, you lose only carry differential.
trades.trigger: HYG -0.1% on Friday's green equity day and flat on the month at the 41st percentile, versus BKLN +0.5% on the month and in an uptrend; credit & vol composite still -63, the worst on the board.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaiming its 1-month highs (z back above 0) or HY making new relative highs versus Treasuries for a week.
trades.target: 300-400bp of pair return; HYG/IEF toward the 30th percentile.

trades.name: Long homebuilders on the duration rally
trades.line: Long ITB: 10y -42bp on the month, housing relative strength +20%
trades.expr: Long ITB, or long DHI outright. Keep it small until the 30y mortgage breaks 7.00%.
trades.thesis: The 42bp rally in the 10y and 41bp in the 30y over the month has not yet passed through to the mortgage rate, which is only -10bp at 7.18%. That gap closes with a lag, and builders are already discounting it.
trades.trigger: ITB +14.0% on the month at z=1.68 and turning up, XHB/SPY +13.9% on the month at z=2.57, DHI +14.3%, HD +20.2% at z=2.79, with TLT +6.2% on the month at acceleration z=2.07.
trades.stop: 10y back above 5.05% or the 30y mortgage making a new high above 7.30%; ITB losing 92.
